steps.title: Germany
steps.body: Germany is the world's third largest Pinot Noir producer, after France and the US, as Spätburgunder. Warmer vintages and better winemaking have transformed it since the 1990s. Baden, the Pfalz and the Ahr make elegant, increasingly respected wines, some rivalling good Burgundy.

steps.title: Oregon and California
steps.body: Oregon's Willamette Valley, at Burgundy's latitude, makes Pinot Noir with bright fruit and earthy notes. In California, the Sonoma Coast, Russian River Valley, Santa Rita Hills and Anderson Valley, cooled by ocean fog and wind, give riper, fuller styles. The 2004 film Sideways boosted US Pinot sales.

steps.prompt: Match each region to its Pinot Noir.
steps.explanation: Cool climates around the world grow fine Pinot.

steps.title: New Zealand
steps.body: Pinot Noir is New Zealand's most planted red. Central Otago, the southernmost major wine region, gives vivid, fruity wines with fresh acidity. Martinborough gives savoury, structured wines; Marlborough lighter, fruit-driven ones. Australia's Yarra Valley, Mornington and Tasmania also excel.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Germany's Spätburgunder is now respected worldwide
Oregon and coastal California make fine Pinot
New Zealand's Central Otago leads the southern hemisphere
